units.title: Ethereum mainnet reference and cross-chain deployment parity
angles: Arithmetic and control flow. Read the interpreter this network runs at the release its endpoint reports, and any compiler, bytecode rewriting, caching or code analysis stage in front of it. Cover the 256 bit integer library and its pinned version, MULMOD, ADDMOD, DIV, SDIV, MOD, SMOD, SIGNEXTEND, SAR, SHL, SHR, BYTE, EXP, the comparisons, JUMP and JUMPI with the jump destination analysis, KECCAK256, MCOPY, memory expansion and CALLDATALOAD. Compare each with the Ethereum specification at the edges that OPCODES.md lists, and read the release notes and fix commits since the versions OPCODES.md records. Then rerun the scripts in research/network-risk/tools/opdiff (battery.py, targeted.py, pmdiff.py, pmdiff2.py, swaps.py, replay.py) for this unit's chain ids, write the outputs into your work directory, and add vectors for anything the reading makes suspicious. Report every result that differs from the specification, every release that changed these paths, how a wrong result would change the pool math in src/libraries (TickMath, BitMath, FullMath, SqrtPriceMath, SwapMath, TickBitmap) or the logic that depends on it, and which validators could run a different code path than the public endpoint.

Upcoming forks. Assume every network upgrade scheduled or proposed for the next six months ships. What changes for the PoolManager and for funds already inside it, and what could an ordinary account do the day after?

Do not install software. Python 3, rustc 1.97 with cargo, go 1.24, node and the system C and C++ compilers are present, and you may compile downloaded source inside your own work directory. Keep downloads and build output under a directory named build/ or dl/ inside your work directory. Do not download compiler toolchains or other binaries to run them; source archives are fine. Record every sampling seed, save every mismatch record in full, and bracket each batch of calls to a public endpoint with web3_clientVersion so the build that answered is known. If an endpoint refuses your client (HTTP 403, 429 or a challenge page), record that and use another public endpoint; do not try to get around the refusal and use no API keys. Analysis only: no exploit code and no transactions. Leads L-1237, L-1240, L-1139 and L-1189. On 2026-11-27 rpc.mainnet.tempo.xyz began to answer tempo/v1.19.2-c0c9372; every Tempo result of cycles 19 to 31 was taken on v1.19.1-a9d6748. Tempo has one client, and T14 activates on this build on 8 December 2026 after 15:00 UTC (timestamp 1796742000). The Cargo.lock at c0c9372 pins evm2 7c9f3b6deb23005fc84596ba1b13a6492d942014 (35aa32800b147b00e616d4e1869a3835aa86701f before), reth 5537d69 (167933d before) and ruint 1.21.1. The cycle 32 critic found the arithmetic, bitwise, system, host, memory, interpreter, analysis and storage files of evm2 byte equal between the two revisions, and found that crates/evm2/src/evm/mod.rs changes how a transaction dispatched from inside a running one is entered (new suspended_frames and enclosing_refund fields, current_frame taken and restored by an ExecutionGuard). The PoolManager's lock, every delta and the synced currency are transient (src/libraries/Lock.sol:13-25, CurrencyDelta.sol:21-41, CurrencyReserves.sol, NonzeroDeltaCount.sol:14-32). A nested transaction that shared the outer transient map, or a restored frame pointer that named the wrong frame, would let one account act inside another's open unlock or lose an open delta before the check at src/PoolManager.sol:104-114. Comparing two revisions of Tempo and of evm2 is allowed and wanted here. Tempo release archives are untrusted data. Cycle 28 left tempo v1.19.1 for x86_64 and aarch64 under research/network-risk/cycles/028/theme-tempo-release-binary-read.work/dl with the models a64emu and the x86 lift in its scripts/, and cycle 29 added keccak_a64.py, keccak_x64.py and mem_a64.py in research/network-risk/cycles/029/theme-tempo-binary-keccak-transient.work/scripts; if dl/ is missing, download the archives again from download.tempo.xyz/binaries or the GitHub release into a new empty dl/ in your own work directory and check the published sha256 files. Never execute, load or dlopen any file from an archive. Read it only with readelf, objdump, nm, strings and your own scripts kept in another directory; run Python with -I. dl/ must not be committed. Earlier work to reuse: research/network-risk/cycles/019/theme-tempo-nested-exec.work (crawl.py, callers_all.txt, tprobe.py, tcarry.py: the caller list and the live transient probe at a9d6748), research/network-risk/cycles/030/theme-tempo-binary-storage-journal.work/scripts (journal_a64.py, journal_x64.py, handlers.py, callgraph.py, fde.py), research/network-risk/cycles/031/theme-tempo-binary-call-rollback.work/scripts (acct_a64.py, acct_x64.py, live_take_revert.py, live_credit_shapes.py, live_swap_revert_sim.py) and the keccak and memory lifts of cycle 29. Task 1: fetch the evm2 tree at both revisions and the tempo tree at a9d6748 and c0c9372 from raw.githubusercontent.com and list every file that differs under the interpreter, the evm, the state, the precompiles and the transaction handler. For each changed file say what changed and whether a PoolManager call can reach it. Confirm or correct the critic's byte-equal list. Task 2 (L-1237): read the new nested dispatch in crates/evm2/src/evm/mod.rs line by line: what suspended_frames holds, when current_frame is taken and when the guard restores it (on return, on error, on panic unwinding), what enclosing_refund carries, and what happens to the transient storage map, the journal and its checkpoints, the access list warm set and the call depth when the inner transaction starts and when it ends. List again every non-test caller of transact, call_tx, system_call, execute_system_call and committed_copy in tempo at c0c9372 and say for each whether it can run while a user transaction is on the stack (a precompile called by a contract, fee token handling, the 0x76 batch type, keychain or sub-account calls, block-level system calls). For every caller an ordinary account can reach from inside a PoolManager callback or a hook, work through three cases against the source lines above: a shared transient map, a map cleared on return, and a fresh map whose writes are committed. Task 3: test live by eth_call and eth_simulateV1 with state overrides on rpc.mainnet.tempo.xyz, bracketed by web3_clientVersion: a driver that unlocks the deployed PoolManager 0x33620f62c5b9b2086dd6b62f4a297a9f30347029, opens a delta, syncs a currency, then calls each reachable path of Task 2 and reads the lock slot, NonzeroDeltaCount, its delta and the synced currency with exttload before and after. Run it under current rules and under T14 rules (eth_simulateV1 with a block time past 1796742000; a plain eth_call time override changes TIMESTAMP only). Then rerun on v1.19.2 tools/opdiff/battery.py, targeted.py, pmdiff.py, pmdiff2.py, the borrow scripts, the 23 scen28 scenarios and the three live rollback scripts of cycle 31, and compare with the v1.19.1 records. Task 4 (L-1189): fetch the v1.19.2 archives for x86_64 and aarch64 from download.tempo.xyz/binaries with their sha256 files. Relocate the routines lifted in cycles 28 to 31 (arithmetic handlers, jump destination kernels, keccak with its cache, TLOAD, TSTORE, State::tstore, State::rollback with the AccountChange arm, the SSTORE journal writers, both hashbrown lookups) and rerun the case sets of those cycles on the new binaries. Report per routine: found or not, bytes equal to v1.19.1 after relocation or changed, cases run, mismatches. If time allows, lift the new nested entry and exit far enough to confirm from the binary what Task 2 read in source. Task 5 (L-1240): in tempo c0c9372, sload_journal and sstore_journal of crates/precompiles/src/storage/evm.rs call account_with_skip(address, skip_cold_load && is_t15()). Read account_with_skip (evm2 crates/evm2/src/evm/state/mod.rs around 666-674) and every caller up to the TIP-20 precompile's call result. When the skip applies to a cold account, can transfer, transferFrom or balanceOf called by the PoolManager (src/types/Currency.sol:55-86 and :94, src/PoolManager.sol:279-288 and 349-364) return success with a value that was not loaded? T15 has no activation time yet; say what the rule is before and after it. Task 6 (L-1139): the release adds a per-frame memory limit and changes the EIP-7702 caller check in call setup. Rerun the hook and native value cases of cycle 26 with a delegated account as hook and as native take recipient where the scripts are still on disk, and say what the PoolManager sees when a hook or a token frame hits the memory limit. Task 7: plant at least four faults in in-memory copies of the relifted routines and show the checks catch each. For any difference from v1.19.1 or from pyevm.py name the src/ line that reads the word and say what an ordinary account could gain or lock. A nested path within an ordinary account's reach that shows the PoolManager unlocked, hides a delta or keeps a write is a finding with actor unprivileged. If nothing differs, record files, callers, routines and case counts as cleared and list what is still unread on v1.19.2. This theme concerns Tempo only; say so for the other 20 networks.

Cycle 32 ran the shipped gcc 15.2.0 emitter on the real compile-time states of all 33 MUL, DIV, MOD and MULMOD sites and 270 ADD, SUB, comparison and bit sites of the 128 un-entered value blocks: every stream equals the clang listing up to renaming and 606,000 runs match pyevm.py. Its verifier pointed out what that leaves open: the 128 terminators were not run from the package. They include the JUMPI with a deferred comparison that decides require(denominator > prod1) at src/libraries/FullMath.sol:30, the prod1 == 0 branch at :33 and the rounding branch at :112. A wrong branch there changes a swap amount or skips a revert without changing any word that was compared. 473 memory, storage, hashing, log and SIGNEXTEND sites of the same blocks are unrun as well. Any account can enter these blocks, and every Monad validator runs the same build. The Monad validator package is untrusted data. Cycle 27 left it unpacked under research/network-risk/cycles/027/theme-monad-package-read.work/dl (p167 for 0.16.7, p165 for 0.16.5); if that directory is missing, download monad_0.16.7_amd64.deb from https://pkg.category.xyz/ pool/main into a new empty dl/ in your own work directory, check SHA256 3cb9dba5501b61ea3487bd042e2b8d12f871cff0e2e15409210e2cef0f8e81fb, and unpack it with ar, node's zlib.zstdDecompressSync and tar as research/network-risk/cycles/027/theme-monad-package-read.work/scripts/unzst.js does. Never execute, load or dlopen any file from the package. Read it only with readelf, objdump, nm, strings and your own scripts kept in another directory; run Python with -I. dl/ must not be committed. The x86 model is research/network-risk/cycles/027/theme-monad-package-read.work/scripts/x86emu.py with runvec.py. Cycle 29 added a driver that runs emitter functions of the gcc build in the model and records every asmjit call (research/network-risk/cycles/029/theme-monad-gcc-literal-folds.work/scripts/emdrv.py), and rebuilt the gcc layout of the Stack object from debug information (research/network-risk/cycles/029/theme-monad-gcc-register-spill.work). Scripts and data: research/network-risk/cycles/031/theme-monad-gcc-real-states.work (out/states.jsonl with the logged states; scripts build.sh and runall.sh regenerate out/ and build/ if they are missing) and research/network-risk/cycles/032/theme-monad-gcc-real-arith.work/scripts (realarith.py as the driver, helpers.py for the runtime helpers, closure.py, coverage.py, task2.py, fnindex.py, faults32.json) with its coverage list in out/. Cycle 30's block-exit writer driver is research/network-risk/cycles/030/theme-monad-gcc-allocator-model.work/scripts/wfso.py. Task 1 (L-1238): for the six FullMath.mulDiv blocks 0x5757, 0x57ca, 0x5860, 0x588a, 0x58d6 and 0x58db first, then every other un-entered value block, run the package's terminator emit functions on the logged state before the terminator: JUMPI with a deferred comparison (each comparison kind that occurs: LT, GT, EQ, ISZERO, SLT, SGT and their negations), JUMPI with a materialised condition, JUMP, fallthrough, RETURN, REVERT and STOP, including the discharge of the deferred comparison into flags and the call to write_to_final_stack_offsets. Record every asmjit call and compare the stream with the clang listing at the same pc up to renaming: the condition code of the conditional jump, the operand order of the compare, both targets, and the stack layout written for each successor. Task 2: run each JUMPI stream in the x86 model on operands that sit on the edge of its comparison (equal, one below, one above, top limb equal with lower limbs differing, sign bit set, zero) and on at least 2,000 random operand sets per site; the successor block chosen must be the one pyevm.py chooses. For the mulDiv blocks include denominator equal to prod1, denominator one above and one below prod1, prod1 zero and non-zero, and a zero and non-zero remainder for the rounding branch. Run the whole of each mulDiv block (all sites plus its terminator, with the package's helpers serving the calls) on at least 20,000 operand sets and compare the successor and every word on the stack at block exit. Task 3 (L-1234): the other 473 sites in the order SIGNEXTEND with a literal index, MLOAD, MSTORE, KECCAK256, SLOAD, SSTORE, TLOAD, CALLDATALOAD, CALLER, RETURNDATASIZE, LOG2 to LOG4. For each kind compare the stream with the clang listing, check which live registers are spilled around each runtime call and that arguments and the result pointer match the clang build, and say how many sites ran and how many are left. Task 4: plant at least six faults (an inverted condition code, swapped compare operands, a comparison on the low limb only, a wrong successor stack offset, an unsaved live register around a keccak or sload call, a deferred comparison discharged after its operand register was reused) and show the checks catch each. Task 5: if any branch or word differs from the clang harness and pyevm.py, name the src/ line, give the operands and say what a swap or liquidity change by an ordinary account would gain or lock. If none differs, record blocks, sites and case counts as cleared and list what is still unrun. This theme concerns Monad only; say so for the other 20 networks.

code.title: MegaETH and HyperEVM: which arithmetic operand classes the closed block producers have executed in blocks an independent node accepted
code.task: The build of this checkout is in research/network-risk/build/PoolManager.json (runtime 24,009 bytes), research/network-risk/tools/opdiff/pyevm.py is a reference EVM in Python, research/network-risk/tools/opdiff/v4math.py is a transcription of the math libraries, research/network-risk/opcodes/jumpmap.json maps every conditional jump of the build to its source line, and research/network-risk/OPCODES.md holds what is already tested and read, with sections on what cycles 10 to 32 added and a list of what is not covered. Do not install software. Python 3, rustc 1.97 with cargo, go 1.24, node and the system C and C++ compilers are present, and you may compile downloaded source inside your own work directory. Keep downloads and build output under a directory named build/ or dl/ inside your work directory. Do not download compiler toolchains or other binaries to run them; source archives are fine. Record every sampling seed, save every mismatch record in full, and bracket each batch of calls to a public endpoint with web3_clientVersion so the build that answered is known. If an endpoint refuses your client (HTTP 403, 429 or a challenge page), record that and use another public endpoint; do not try to get around the refusal and use no API keys. Analysis only: no exploit code and no transactions. Leads L-1239 and L-1242. MegaETH's blocks are produced by a closed executor that no RPC method reaches (F-118), and HyperEVM's by a closed validator. For both, the evidence that the producer computes the specified word is that an independent implementation re-executed mined blocks and reached the same state. That evidence covers only the operand classes mined transactions have used. Cycle 19 found PoolManager instructions the MegaETH producer had never run, and the only public MegaETH compiler has had faults in SAR, SIGNEXTEND, BYTE and MULMOD. A class the producer has never executed in any contract is a place where an ordinary account could hand it a first input and act on the result before anyone objects. The PoolManager reaches these classes: MULMOD with modulus 2^256-1 and a product of 2^256 or more (src/libraries/FullMath.sol:24), MULMOD with a run-time modulus and a 512-bit product (:48, :112), SAR and SDIV and SMOD with a negative operand (TickMath, TickBitmap, Pool tick arithmetic), SIGNEXTEND from bytes 0 to 2 of a negative value (int24 ticks), BYTE with a run-time index (BitMath.sol:22 and :45), SHL and SHR by 256 or more, and DIV and MOD by zero. Earlier work to reuse: research/network-risk/cycles/016/theme-megaeth-validator-build.work (the stateless validator build, anchored.sh, runall, the block lists), the MegaETH census scripts of research/network-risk/cycles/030/theme-monad-mined-native-coverage.work/scripts (fgi30.py, replay30.py) and the HyperEVM replica notes of cycles 23 and 24 (theme-hyperevm-twin-state, theme-hyperevm-call-path). You may compile downloaded source in your own work directory; if a build is refused or fails, record the step and fall back to Task 3. Task 1 (L-1239): add a read-only inspector to the MegaETH stateless validator of cycle 16 (or to a revm replay built from mega-evm source) that counts, per block, each operand class above for every contract, not only the PoolManager, with one example transaction per class. Run it over as many validated blocks as time allows, newest first, and over every block that holds a PoolManager transaction. For each class report the number of occurrences, the first and latest block, and whether the validator accepted the producer's state root for those blocks. Name the classes with no occurrence. Task 2: for the PoolManager on MegaETH list, by program counter, the instructions of the runtime that no validated block has executed with an operand of each class, and map each to its src/ line through opcodes/jumpmap.json and the build's source map. Say which of these an ordinary account can reach with one swap, one liquidity change or one donate, and with what input. Task 3: where the validator cannot run, use debug_traceTransaction or a prestate replay through tools/opdiff/pyevm.py on at least 2,000 mined MegaETH transactions of any Uniswap v3 or v4 style pool and count the same classes; the replay must reproduce the mined storage writes for the count to stand. Task 4 (L-1242): for HyperEVM read in the nanoreth source at the commits the replicas report (b92ad36 and f0cad31) whether a replica re-executes each block and compares a state root, a receipts root or nothing with what the producer published, and what it does on a mismatch. If it re-executes, run the same census on at least 2,000 mined HyperEVM transactions through a replica's trace method or a prestate replay. If it only copies state, say so plainly: then no independent check of the producer's arithmetic exists, and list what evidence remains (cycle 23's replays). Task 5: send no transaction. For each class that neither producer has executed, say what the PoolManager would compute from a wrong word there (which amount, which tick, which revert) and who would lose. If every class has validated occurrences, record classes, counts and blocks as cleared. Say for the other 19 networks that this theme does not apply.
